To increase the autonomy of space missions across the full Solar System, and thus offloading the overloaded ground stations, ESA is developing a concept for Solar System Internet. Currently, spacecraft navigating in the Solar System rely on explicit, pre-planned setup of point-to-point communication links for their navigation. Such approach, does not scale well with the large number of missions planned in the future. Such a system would combine existing (i.e., GNSS) or planned (i.e., Moonlight, MARCONI) systems and would complement this with dedicated SSI nodes. These nodes would provide ranging capabilities through point-to-point links (as broadcast links are not scalable over long distances). As all spacecraft and SSI nodes are connected (through the Solar System Internet), raw data could be shared, through the decentralized network,enabling more advanced positioning techniques such as collaborative positioning. To achieve this goal, the definition of accurate timescale and reference systems, similar to GNSS or Moonlight, is crucial. The objective of this activity is to study the state-of-the-art concerning time and reference systems applicable to Solar System navigation, assess the gaps and suitability. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Analyse the state-of-the-art of existing Barycentric/planetary reference frames and timescales and the accuracy/availability of transformations between them (e.g., Mars planetocentric to Barycentric) - Investigate how the realizationof existing Barycentric/planetary reference frames can be improved using SSI PNT nodes, pre-selecting the most promising approaches. - Investigate the impact of relativity on Solar System PNT and assess the need for the definition of one (or more) Solar System timescale(s) and the relationship between them, pre-selecting the most promising approaches. - Implement the pre-selected reference frames and timescales, for usage in a Solar System PNT system, in a software simulator, such that end-to-end PNT performance assessment que be performed for the different models and PNT system configurations. - Based on the implemented models in the software simulator, assess the performance and suitability of the pre-selected Barycentric/planetary reference frames and timescales for a Solar System PNT system. - Based on the results obtained via simulation, propose one (or more) Solar System time and reference systems. Description: Objective: To derive a standard set of requirements for the ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) Security Module and implement a prototype form-factor equivalent ADHA module.Description: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) has been initiated through a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primes and data handling equipment suppliers. The initiative has resulted in the agreement on an architecture for data handling unit based on standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined, as well as a standardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development of interoperable modules that can be connected together in ADHA units. More advanced security functions are expected to be required in future ESA missions. The modular format of the proposed solution will enable faster adoption, and verification of new security technologies, in different unit configurations. This activity aims to perform analysis work to derive a standardization of the security function within an ADHA module form-factor, to allow the development of ADHA-compliant security products, which can be utilized together with other existing ADHA products, such as ADHA OBC. When implemented in the ADHA 3U form factor, such units are of particular interest for use in mid-size satellite platforms as well (less than 500kg mass). For prototyping purposes, the target of this activity is an elegant breadboard (EBB) of the ADHA security module in 6U format, based on the security function requirements defined in this activity. The extended format will provide the required design margins for the prototyping and demonstration phase. The long-term goal, this technology development, is the adaptation of this security module to an ADHA 3U module form factor. This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks: - Analyse the use-cases for dedicated security modules in data handling systems, both for platform and payload - Derive the detailed generic requirements for ADHA Security Modules, including functions, performances, electrical and software interfaces, etc. and present the specifications for review of the ADHA consortia and industrial working group - Derive the architectural design of a prototype ADHA Security Module - Derive a prototype electrical and software design of an ADHA Security Module, as an EBB in ADHA 6U format. - Perform functional validation of the prototype and demonstrate a representative use-case for the ADHA Security Module - Derive a roadmap for bringing the derived design to an ADHA 3U security module EM/EQM/FM."}
